text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SEVODNYA
- Russia's biggest commercial banks are showing interest in reviving the country's agriculture.
- The president of Slavneft oil company Anatoly Fomin denied rumours circulating in the Fuel and Energy Ministry about the company's possible merger with Rosneft, SIBUR and other firms.
- The new tax code is being tested now in some regions of Russia. Local authorities may support the new taxation system if it provides for more regional economic independence.
- The State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament defended the interests of gas monopoly Gazprom.
- The Moscow city government is planning to protect the Moskvich car factory against bankruptcy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Strict state controls over personal spending may be introduced in Russia in 1998.
- A unified monetary system between Russia and Belarus is only possible if a federative state is created, says Sergei Dubinin, the head of Russia's Central Bank.
- The State Property Committee is regaining its positions in fighting to reduce state control over the real economy with Alfred Kokh appointed its head.

- Gazprom head Rem Vyakhirev was quick to reassure foreign investors that the company can control the situation with its shares on the ADR market, to prevent any risks before the issue of the second ADR tranche.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The head of Gazprom, Rem Vyakhirev, accused U.S. companies, the IMF and the Russian Finance Ministry of plotting to divide the Russian gas giant.
- Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov says he has President Yeltsin's support in plans to eliminate the system of banks authorised to deal with the federal budget.
- IMF recommends that Russia speed up fight against corruption.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Russian authorities promise to organise and monitor public debates on the Charter of the Russia and Belarus Union closely.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIA
- The West is successfully using Russia's present authorities to destroy the country, says the pro-communist opposition paper.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow may once again face problems with food supplies unless Federal Food Corporation finds the money needed to pay for sufficient food supplies for the city.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
